checks.evidence: Unity's NetCoreRuntime/dotnet.exe + DotNetSdkRoslyn/csc.dll, refs: NetStandard 2.1 netstandard.dll, Managed/UnityEngine/*.dll, libcache template UnityEngine.UI.dll / Unity.InputSystem.dll (copied to evidence/tmp-T8.6/refs). checks.item: Press path: controller primary button to press message
checks.evidence: Read ContextLensXRInput.cs: InputAction bound to <XRController>{LeftHand}/{PrimaryButton} and {RightHand}; started -> OnPrimary -> ContextLensClient.Press() -> socket.Send(PressMessage{request{conversation_id, as_of_seq = last turn seq, detail}}); nothing sent if no transcript yet. Read local toolkit 3.3.0 source: XRSimulatedController : InputSystem.XR.XRController, layout commonUsages LeftHand/RightHand, XRSimulatedControllerState declares primaryButton with usage = "PrimaryButton", SimulatedDeviceLifecycleManager calls SetDeviceUsage(LeftHand/RightHand) on the devices it adds. So a simulator-created device satisfies the binding. The doc states this as 'read from the toolkit 3.3.0 source' and says it has not been run.

Read both: ReceiveStatus/Pause/Resume/DeleteTranscript/close handling are the same rules as Session.receiveStatus/pause/resume/delete/onclose. Beyond reading, I extracted the real method bodies (Handle, ReceiveStatus, Press, SendTestAudio, Pause, Resume, DeleteTranscript, ShowCard, RefreshTranscript, RefreshState, Update) verbatim from ContextLensClient.cs by script into a stub harness (evidence/tmp-T8.6/sm/gen.py, h.cs, prog.cs), compiled with Roslyn, ran on system dotnet 8: 37 checks, ALL OK. Covered: late 'recording' after pause (ignored), after pause ack, while deleting, after deleted, after socket close; Resume without confirmation stays paused/not REC and a second Resume sends nothing; confirmed resume -> REC; resume-pending then close/delete -> recording ignored; REC text only when connection == recording; no audio while paused; press as_of_seq = latest turn; error text shown literally; garbage and unknown-type frames handled. Mutation check of the harness: removing the paused/!resumePending guard produced 4 FAILs; changing the REC label produced FAILs. The harness uses System.Text.Json in place of JsonUtility and stubs Text/Color/socket, so Unity APIs themselves are not exercised.

notes: NOT verified, and cannot be here: the project has never been opened in the Unity Editor (batch mode fails the license check; I did not try to get around it). Editor import, asmdef resolution, Package Manager resolution of XRI 3.3.0 (and its dependencies from the local cache), the real Unity.InputSystem 1.17.0 API (I compiled against the template-cache Unity.InputSystem.dll whose exact version I did not check), JsonUtility behaviour (my harness substitutes System.Text.Json), WebSocket and webcam behaviour at runtime, and the simulator key sequence in unity-setup.md all belong to H3. The press-path and simulator-binding claims are from reading code and the local toolkit source, not from running. The Active Input Handling 'Both' requirement (StandaloneInputModule) is documented. Minor gaps, not failures: (1) the checker only refuses the literal text '[Serializable]' outside Messages.cs, so '[System.Serializable]' in another file would not be flagged (I confirmed: MISSED); nothing in the repo does this. (2) The checker raises UnicodeDecodeError rather than a clean message on a non-UTF8 Messages.cs (still nonzero). (3) The checker does not look at client logic; the indicator rules are protected only by reading and by my out-of-repo harness, so the repo has no regression test for them (the doc says so). (4) docs/client-contract.md line 15 vs line 32 on a 'paused' reply is the known ambiguity routed elsewhere; the client works with either behaviour. The one full-suite failure is the known T5.1-not-merged test. My Roslyn scripts and harness are in orchestration/evidence/tmp-T8.6/ (refs/, sm/, base.rsp, mut3.py).
